/inspection/piping-inspection-services-a.html:
Piping inspection in Atlanta

Plan piping inspection in Atlanta around the equipment condition and the decision the owner needs to make. Start with the asset register, inspection history and access constraints; these determine the examination scope. Site attendance, personnel and equipment are confirmed in the proposal.

Define the inspection question

For piping, separate a wall-loss survey from a weld examination. A thickness reading can support corrosion trending at a recorded location; it does not demonstrate that a weld is free from cracking. Identify the service, material, line number, nominal wall and known damage mechanisms before choosing the method.

Mark the inspection locations on an isometric or a consistent asset map. Record insulation, coatings, supports and inaccessible areas. Repeating a measurement at a different point can produce an apparent change that is caused by location rather than deterioration.

Choose methods for the expected damage

Ultrasonic thickness measurement is useful for accessible wall-thickness readings. Surface methods may be appropriate for accessible surface-breaking indications, while weld examinations require a defined technique and coverage. Screening methods help locate areas for follow-up; their limitations must be carried into the report.

Agree the governing standard, adopted edition, owner specification and acceptance criteria with the responsible personnel. Listing several codes in a report does not establish that all of them apply. A Level III procedure review and an owner’s engineering assessment have different responsibilities.

Prepare the site and records

For a site visit in Atlanta, provide the site contact, work window, access arrangements and permit requirements before mobilisation. Identify work at height, confined-space entry, insulation removal and any operating restrictions. Do not assume that access preparation or isolation is included unless it is written into the scope.

Provide previous measurements in a usable register, with units, dates and location references. Flag repairs, replaced sections and changes in service. If historical records cannot be matched to the current asset, keep that uncertainty visible instead of treating the values as a reliable trend.

Agree the handover before work starts

A useful handover identifies the equipment, examination locations, technique, applicable procedure revision, personnel, instrument records, results and coverage limitations. Photos and marked drawings should use the same references as the result table. Keep inaccessible areas separate from areas examined with no reportable indication.

Ask for the report format and review responsibilities in the quotation. Include the route for resolving incomplete coverage or unexpected findings. The final package should make it possible for the owner to understand what was examined, repeat the work and decide what follow-up is needed.

/digital-twins/data-center.html:
Digital twins for data centre

A data-centre model is most useful when an operator can move from an equipment tag to the maintenance history without searching several systems. Start with the cooling or electrical assets that cause the most difficult handovers.

Build the asset hierarchy

Cooling loops, pumps, heat exchangers and accessible pipework form the starting structure for this use case. Agree the naming rules with the people who maintain the equipment register. A model identifier should remain stable when a drawing is revised or a new inspection is added.

Connect records to decisions

Link the equipment register to location, maintenance responsibility and dated inspection records. Keep live operating measurements separate from one-off inspection readings; they have different sampling, accuracy and ownership.

Define who can upload, review and approve information. Keep draft observations visibly separate from approved records. Agree how the model will reference the existing maintenance or document system and who will resolve mismatches.

Make limitations visible

A scan of a plant room can locate pipework and access routes. It cannot establish internal condition, electrical safety or cooling capacity. Each of those questions needs its own evidence.

Run a useful acceptance exercise

Choose a maintainable asset group, such as a cooling loop. Check that a technician can locate an item, retrieve its latest approved record, add a new observation and identify an outstanding action.

Record the steps that still require manual work. Before extending the scope, agree ownership of updates, access permissions, backups, exports and support. The acceptance exercise should demonstrate the proposed workflow using representative records.

Digital twins for nuclear plant

A nuclear-plant digital twin should begin with controlled asset identification and document ownership. A visually detailed model is of limited use if it points to an obsolete drawing or an unapproved inspection record.

Build the asset hierarchy

Equipment tags, controlled drawings and inspection locations form the starting structure for this use case. Agree the naming rules with the people who maintain the equipment register. A model identifier should remain stable when a drawing is revised or a new inspection is added.

Connect records to decisions

Retain procedure revisions, examination dates, qualification records and approval history with the underlying result. Distinguish a planning view from the plant’s controlled record system. Agree access, hosting and change control with the owner before any data transfer.

Define who can upload, review and approve information. Keep draft observations visibly separate from approved records. Agree how the model will reference the existing maintenance or document system and who will resolve mismatches.

Make limitations visible

The model does not establish regulatory acceptance, qualification for an examination or permission to use inspection data in a safety decision. Those responsibilities remain with the plant’s approved arrangements.

Run a useful acceptance exercise

Use a bounded, approved set of records to test traceability from an equipment tag to its source document and review decision. Include a superseded record and verify that it remains distinguishable from the current version.

Digital twins for petrochemical complex

In a petrochemical complex, the first useful digital-twin question is often simple: which equipment does this inspection result belong to, and what has changed since the last examination? A consistent asset hierarchy makes that answer possible.

Build the asset hierarchy

Process units, equipment tags, line numbers and corrosion monitoring locations form the starting structure for this use case. Agree the naming rules with the people who maintain the equipment register. A model identifier should remain stable when a drawing is revised or a new inspection is added.

Connect records to decisions

Keep inspection readings connected to their dates, units and actual locations. Record repairs, replacements and changes of service so a trend is not calculated across unlike conditions. Link findings to an accountable action owner.

Define who can upload, review and approve information. Keep draft observations visibly separate from approved records. Agree how the model will reference the existing maintenance or document system and who will resolve mismatches.

Make limitations visible

A coloured model is a presentation of the underlying data. It does not establish a damage mechanism, a remaining-life value or fitness for service without the necessary technical assessment.

Run a useful acceptance exercise

Select a unit with an existing inspection history. Reconcile the asset list, import a reviewed sample and ask inspectors and planners to locate the same finding independently.

Record the steps that still require manual work. Before extending the scope, agree ownership of updates, access permissions, backups, exports and support. The acceptance exercise should demonstrate the proposed workflow using representative records.

Pipeline inspection data needs a stable location reference. A digital twin can bring route geometry, inspection locations and follow-up records into the same view, provided each dataset can be traced back to its source.

Build the asset hierarchy

Line segments, chainage or stationing, joints and examination locations form the starting structure for this use case. Agree the naming rules with the people who maintain the equipment register. A model identifier should remain stable when a drawing is revised or a new inspection is added.

Connect records to decisions

Define the coordinate system, distance convention and asset identifiers before combining surveys. Preserve the original result and any transformation used to place it on the model. Note areas where the position is approximate.

Define who can upload, review and approve information. Keep draft observations visibly separate from approved records. Agree how the model will reference the existing maintenance or document system and who will resolve mismatches.

Make limitations visible

A surface survey does not measure wall loss. Different inspection technologies also have different coverage and sizing limits; placing them on one map does not remove those differences.

Run a useful acceptance exercise

Pick a segment with known reference points and approved inspection data. Test how a reviewer finds an indication, opens the source report and records a follow-up action without losing its location reference.

/glossary/false-indication.html:
A suspected false indication needs a recorded explanation. Do not erase a result simply because it does not fit the expected pattern.

Separate the observation from its cause

First record the indication and the examination conditions. Check equipment function, surface preparation, consumables, geometry and the applicable procedure. A response caused by part geometry is not the same as an equipment artefact, even when neither represents a defect.

Repeat or extend the examination only within the approved procedure. If the result remains unclear, refer it to the responsible qualified reviewer and retain both the original observation and the follow-up evidence.

Use careful reporting language

State what was seen, what checks were performed and the basis for the conclusion. Avoid writing “no defect” where the actual conclusion is that the original response could not be reproduced or that coverage was limited.

A useful record allows another inspector to understand the decision without reconstructing the work from memory. Include the location reference, settings or technique information needed to reproduce the examination.

/integrations/aspen-mtell.html:
Scoping an Atlantis integration with Aspen Mtell

An integration with Aspen Mtell is an implementation project. Confirm the required data flow, access rights and supported interfaces before treating it as part of the purchased solution. A named integration page is not proof of a prebuilt connector.

Define the records and ownership

Start with equipment identifiers, inspection observations and maintenance events. For each record, agree which system owns it, the identifier used to match it, the fields to transfer and when an update should occur. Keep the initial scope limited enough to test using representative data.

Read access and write access are different requirements. Ask the administrators of both systems to confirm the available interface, authentication method and permitted operations. Additional vendor licences or configuration may be necessary.

Test failure and reconciliation

Include duplicate records, missing identifiers, rejected updates and interrupted transfers in the acceptance test. Decide where failures are recorded and who can retry or correct them. A successful demonstration with one record does not establish that a recurring transfer is reliable.

Confirm how approved records, attachments, timestamps and status changes will be handled. Document the support boundary between Atlantis, the customer and the other software provider before the connection goes into service.

/ndt-career-guide.html:
Start with the work you want to perform and the qualification scheme your intended employer uses. Course completion, industrial experience, examination and authorisation are separate steps.

Choose a route from the job requirements

Read current job descriptions in your target region and list the methods, levels and sector requirements that recur. Ask employers whether they use an employer-based programme or require independent certification. A course advertised as “Level II” does not by itself establish that you meet either route.

Choose a method because it is relevant to the work and you can obtain suitable practical training and supervised experience. Compare course scope, instructor support, practical access and examination arrangements before paying.

Keep records from the beginning

Retain training records, examination results and documented experience with enough detail for the responsible reviewer to assess them. Record the employer, method, duties, dates and supervision required by the applicable scheme.

Atlantis courses are primarily self-paced, with year-round enrolment and Level III clarification support. Confirm practical sessions and assessment arrangements separately. Use a pathway consultation to identify gaps in your existing evidence before selecting the next course.

/ndt-connect-platform.html:
An inspection platform should make the handover between technician, reviewer and customer easier to follow. Judge it using a real job and the records your team needs to retain.

Follow a report through its working life

Begin with a work order and a defined asset. Record the assigned technician, equipment and procedure before entering results. Check how a reviewer returns a report for correction and how an approved version is kept separate from the working draft.

Ask what the customer can view or download, how access is withdrawn and how a corrected report is communicated. These decisions affect the workflow as much as the layout of the report.

Confirm the product and access scope

Use the demonstration to confirm which Atlantis product supplies the workflow, what access is available today and which parts require configuration. Do not assume that every named service or portal shares the same user account or subscription.

Ask for a written scope covering records, user roles, exports, support and any connection to another system. Bring one current report template and an anonymised example job so the discussion can focus on your actual process.

/ndt-for-aerospace.html:
Aerospace NDT requirements depend on the part, material, manufacturing or maintenance stage, and the controlling customer documents. A list of methods alone is not an inspection plan.

Identify the controlling documents

Start with the part number, drawing revision, process specification and any customer-approved technique requirements. Establish who approves procedures and personnel, and whether the work falls within a manufacturing or maintenance quality system.

Magnetic-particle testing applies to ferromagnetic materials. Penetrant testing addresses accessible surface-breaking discontinuities on suitable nonporous surfaces. Ultrasonic, eddy-current and radiographic examinations answer different questions and require a technique suited to the part.

Keep qualification and acceptance separate

A personnel certificate does not replace the employer’s authorisation or the customer’s process approval. Likewise, a method standard may describe how to examine a part without providing the acceptance limits for that particular component.

Before booking training or review work, provide the intended method, level, sector and governing personnel scheme. Agree practical equipment and specimen needs, examination responsibilities and the records required for the employer’s decision.

/ndt-methods.html:
Method selection starts with the discontinuity or condition you need to detect, the material, the geometry and the available access. No single method answers every inspection question.

Surface and internal examination

Visual examination establishes accessible surface condition and helps direct further work. Penetrant testing can reveal suitable surface-breaking discontinuities on nonporous materials; magnetic-particle testing is limited to ferromagnetic materials. Surface preparation and access affect both.

Ultrasonic and radiographic techniques can examine internal conditions, but orientation, geometry, resolution and coverage differ. Eddy-current techniques depend on electrical conductivity and a suitable setup. A method name does not define the achievable detection capability for a particular part.

Write the technique and reporting requirements

Record what must be covered, what access is available and what limitations will remain. Agree the applicable procedure, reference checks, personnel requirements and acceptance criteria before the examination begins.

For example, a thickness survey intended to trend corrosion needs repeatable measurement locations. A weld examination intended to detect planar discontinuities needs a technique and coverage appropriate to that objective. The same instrument cannot make those scopes interchangeable.

/resources-downloads.html:
Choose a resource for the decision or record you need to prepare. Templates, calculators and study material can help organise work, but they do not replace an approved procedure, current standard or responsible technical review.

Templates and records

Before using a template, identify the asset, procedure revision, required fields and approval route. Remove examples and complete the document with actual records. Keep the blank master under revision control so later jobs do not reuse an obsolete copy.

A calibration certificate template is a record format. It does not establish calibration traceability or authorise a person to issue a laboratory certificate. Link completed records to the underlying evidence and the organisation responsible for the work.

Calculators and learning tools

Check units, assumptions and the intended range of use before relying on a calculated result. Retain the inputs with the output and obtain technical review where the calculation supports an inspection or operational decision.

Browser practice tools are useful for learning instrument concepts. They do not establish supervised industrial experience or practical competence. Follow the training and examination arrangements required by the employer or relevant certification body.

/verticals.html:
Industry context changes the inspection scope. Begin with the asset, its service, the expected damage and the requirements named by the owner or customer. Use the sector guides to organise the questions before requesting a proposal.

Operating assets and maintenance

For operating plants, provide the asset register, service history and previous examination records. Explain whether the work supports routine monitoring, a shutdown, repair planning or investigation of a finding. These purposes may require different methods and deliverables.

For marine, offshore or remote work, identify access, permits, environmental constraints and who will prepare the asset. Mobilisation and specialist resources are agreed for the project, rather than assumed from a regional service page.

Manufacturing and fabrication

For new equipment or fabrication, provide the drawing, material, weld details and controlling specification. Identify hold points and the parties responsible for procedure approval, witnessing and final acceptance.

A report should distinguish the areas examined from exclusions or inaccessible locations. Agree the required drawing references, result format and handover package before work starts. This makes the quotation and the eventual review easier to assess.

/inspection/piping-inspection-services-a.html:
Piping inspection in Abu Dhabi

Plan piping inspection in Abu Dhabi around the equipment condition and the decision the owner needs to make. Start with the asset register, inspection history and access constraints; these determine the examination scope. Site attendance, personnel and equipment are confirmed in the proposal.

Define the inspection question

For piping, separate a wall-loss survey from a weld examination. A thickness reading can support corrosion trending at a recorded location; it does not demonstrate that a weld is free from cracking. Identify the service, material, line number, nominal wall and known damage mechanisms before choosing the method.

Mark the inspection locations on an isometric or a consistent asset map. Record insulation, coatings, supports and inaccessible areas. Repeating a measurement at a different point can produce an apparent change that is caused by location rather than deterioration.

Choose methods for the expected damage

Ultrasonic thickness measurement is useful for accessible wall-thickness readings. Surface methods may be appropriate for accessible surface-breaking indications, while weld examinations require a defined technique and coverage. Screening methods help locate areas for follow-up; their limitations must be carried into the report.

Agree the governing standard, adopted edition, owner specification and acceptance criteria with the responsible personnel. Listing several codes in a report does not establish that all of them apply. A Level III procedure review and an owner’s engineering assessment have different responsibilities.

Prepare the site and records

For a site visit in Abu Dhabi, provide the site contact, work window, access arrangements and permit requirements before mobilisation. Identify work at height, confined-space entry, insulation removal and any operating restrictions. Do not assume that access preparation or isolation is included unless it is written into the scope.

Provide previous measurements in a usable register, with units, dates and location references. Flag repairs, replaced sections and changes in service. If historical records cannot be matched to the current asset, keep that uncertainty visible instead of treating the values as a reliable trend.

Agree the handover before work starts

A useful handover identifies the equipment, examination locations, technique, applicable procedure revision, personnel, instrument records, results and coverage limitations. Photos and marked drawings should use the same references as the result table. Keep inaccessible areas separate from areas examined with no reportable indication.

Ask for the report format and review responsibilities in the quotation. Include the route for resolving incomplete coverage or unexpected findings. The final package should make it possible for the owner to understand what was examined, repeat the work and decide what follow-up is needed.

/eddy-current-testing-bangalore.html:
Prepare a useful eddy-current examination scope

Confirm that the material is electrically conductive. Identify whether the task concerns surface cracking, tubing, material sorting or another defined application. Provide geometry, material condition, surface coating and expected access before selecting a probe and technique.

Understand the technique limitations

Reference standards, frequency, probe selection and lift-off affect the response. Geometry, conductivity and permeability changes can also produce signals. A setup developed for one component should not be assumed suitable for a different material or discontinuity orientation.

Specify the records and review

Record the reference standard, setup, coverage and limitations with the examination results. Retain the relevant signals and location references where the technique requires them. Confirm how ambiguous responses will be investigated and who makes the acceptance decision.

For background, see ASNT’s method overview. Discuss procedure and personnel requirements before confirming the work.

/magnetic-particle-testing-beaumont.html:
Prepare a useful magnetic-particle examination scope

First confirm that the material is ferromagnetic. Provide the component geometry, accessible surfaces and likely discontinuity orientation. The inspection technique must establish suitable field direction and examination conditions for the area concerned.

Understand the technique limitations

MT addresses surface and near-surface discontinuities in suitable materials. It does not measure remaining wall thickness or provide a general volumetric assessment. Coatings, surface condition and geometry can affect the examination and the interpretation of indications.

Specify the records and review

Record the technique, examination area, applicable checks and indication locations. Agree any cleaning or demagnetisation requirements. Evaluate reportable indications using the specified acceptance criteria rather than treating every particle accumulation as a rejectable defect.

For background, see ASNT’s method overview. Discuss procedure and personnel requirements before confirming the work.

Confirm a suitable nonporous surface and an examination objective involving surface-breaking discontinuities. Provide the material, surface finish, temperature conditions and any restrictions on inspection materials or cleaning products.

Understand the technique limitations

The approved technique governs preparation, penetrant application, removal, development and examination conditions. Contamination, smeared surfaces or unsuitable preparation can obstruct openings. Penetrant inspection cannot establish the condition of discontinuities that do not open to the examined surface.

Specify the records and review

Keep part identity, examination area, material system, procedure revision and indication locations in the report. Separate the observation of an indication from its evaluation against the specified acceptance criteria. Agree post-examination cleaning and handling with the owner.

For background, see ASNT’s method overview. Discuss procedure and personnel requirements before confirming the work.

/radiographic-testing-bangalore.html:
Prepare a useful radiographic examination scope

Provide the material, section thickness, weld or component drawing and the required image coverage. State whether the project permits film, computed radiography or digital detector techniques, and identify the controlling acceptance document.

Understand the technique limitations

Source and detector access, object geometry and discontinuity orientation affect what an image can show. Radiography uses ionising radiation. An appropriately authorised provider must plan radiation protection and access controls under the applicable local requirements. A service enquiry is not a radiation-safety plan.

Specify the records and review

Agree image identification, image-quality evidence, interpretation responsibilities and retention before work starts. The report should identify the areas imaged and any limitations; a retained image does not establish coverage of an entire component.

For background, see ASNT’s method overview. Discuss procedure and personnel requirements before confirming the work.

/ultrasonic-testing-baton-rouge.html:
Prepare a useful ultrasonic examination scope

A thickness survey and a weld examination need different setups. For a thickness survey, supply nominal dimensions, material and repeatable measurement locations. For welds, provide the joint drawing, thickness, access and the discontinuities the technique must detect.

Understand the technique limitations

Check that the selected probe, reference standard and scan coverage suit the geometry. Coupling, surface condition, temperature and material structure can affect the response. An A-scan is a signal to interpret within the approved technique; a peak alone does not identify the cause.

Specify the records and review

Keep the location reference, calibration or reference checks, instrument settings and coverage limitations with the results. A corrosion trend is meaningful only when successive measurements refer to comparable locations and conditions.

For background, see ASNT’s method overview. Discuss procedure and personnel requirements before confirming the work.

/visual-testing-beaumont.html:
Prepare a useful visual examination scope

Agree what must be examined and what constitutes a reportable condition. Supply drawings, weld or component identification, accessible surfaces and the acceptance document. Identify whether the examination is direct or requires an optical aid or remote system.

Understand the technique limitations

Access, lighting, viewing angle and surface condition affect the examination. A photograph can preserve an observation, but it may not establish dimensions, scale or coverage by itself. Visual examination of an accessible surface does not demonstrate the absence of internal damage.

Specify the records and review

Use a consistent location reference for observations and photographs. Include a scale where it is relevant and record inaccessible areas separately. Have the responsible reviewer decide which findings require measurement, another NDT method, repair assessment or follow-up.

For background, see ASNT’s method overview. Discuss procedure and personnel requirements before confirming the work.

Use a consistent location reference for observations and photographs. Include a scale where it is relevant and record inaccessible areas separately. Have the responsible reviewer decide which findings require measurement, another NDT method, repair assessment or follow-up.

/digital-twins/refinery.title: Digital twins for refinery inspection | Atlantis NDT
/digital-twins/refinery.description: A refinery digital twin should help an inspection team find and interpret the records behind a maintenance decision.
/digital-twins/refinery.html:
Digital twins for refinery inspection

A refinery digital twin should help an inspection team find and interpret the records behind a maintenance decision. Start with a defined asset and a reliable inspection history. The model provides context for evidence; it does not replace the examination or the engineering assessment.

Set up a usable asset structure

Bring together piping circuits, equipment tags, measurement locations and inspection history. Agree identifiers before importing files. The same location should have the same reference in the drawing, measurement table and model, so a later survey can be compared with the original record.

Preserve the source and examination limits

Attach the inspection date, method, procedure reference, units and review status to each result. Keep links to the original report and supporting files. Show inaccessible areas and incomplete coverage explicitly; an area without a result must not look like an area examined without a finding.

Separate measured condition from interpretation

Keep actual observations distinct from calculated trends and engineering recommendations. Before comparing measurements, check that location, method and measurement conditions are sufficiently consistent. A colour change in a model should have a stated basis that the reviewer can trace and understand.

Evaluate the workflow on one asset

Ask the inspector and planner to use representative records to establish which records support the proposed turnaround work. Test whether they can retrieve the source report, identify its revision and distinguish an open finding from a completed action. Record where the proposed workflow still needs manual reconciliation.

Agree ownership and acceptance

Name the people responsible for asset identifiers, data upload, technical review and closing actions. Confirm access permissions, exports, backups and how corrections are recorded. Agree any link to the existing maintenance or document system as a separate implementation scope, including data mapping and failure handling.

/magnetic-particle-testing-atlanta.html:
Prepare a useful magnetic-particle examination scope

First confirm that the material is ferromagnetic. Provide the component geometry, accessible surfaces and likely discontinuity orientation. The inspection technique must establish suitable field direction and examination conditions for the area concerned.

Understand the technique limitations

MT addresses surface and near-surface discontinuities in suitable materials. It does not measure remaining wall thickness or provide a general volumetric assessment. Coatings, surface condition and geometry can affect the examination and the interpretation of indications.

Specify the records and review

Record the technique, examination area, applicable checks and indication locations. Agree any cleaning or demagnetisation requirements. Evaluate reportable indications using the specified acceptance criteria rather than treating every particle accumulation as a rejectable defect.

For background, see ASNT’s method overview. Discuss procedure and personnel requirements before confirming the work.

/ndt-erp-argentina.html:
NDT ERP evaluation in Argentina

Evaluate Atlantis NDT ERP against the work your inspection company performs in Argentina. Use a representative job and agreed acceptance tasks to establish whether the proposed configuration fits your operation.

Start with the inspection job

Bring a redacted report, a typical quotation and the records used to dispatch a crew. Follow the work through technician selection, equipment availability, result capture, review and invoicing. Record who makes each decision and which information must be carried to the next step.

Verify the personnel and equipment records

Ask the demonstrator to show method and level alongside the certification scheme and validity dates. Check how vision-test records and equipment calibration references are retrieved. An expiry reminder is useful, but the responsible employer still decides whether the person is authorised for the assignment.

Test report corrections and customer delivery

Create a report with an intentional omission, return it for correction and approve the revised version. Check what the customer can see, how an obsolete report is identified and whether the final export includes the references your customer requires. Keep the original inspection evidence with the approved result.

Define the regional implementation scope

Confirm contracting, support hours, hosting, access permissions and any onsite work for your organisation. Check required language, date and unit formats using your own templates. This is a product evaluation guide, not evidence of a local office or of approval by a regulator or customer.

Plan imports and external connections

Clean duplicate personnel, customer and equipment identifiers before a trial import. Keep source files and reconcile record counts after the import. For accounting or maintenance software, agree which system owns each field and how failed transfers are corrected. External connections are scoped through the available interfaces; a product name alone does not establish a working integration.

Agree trial acceptance

The owner has confirmed a 14-day ERP trial. Before it starts, agree the users, data, modules, setup assistance and evaluation tasks included. Write down the conditions for a successful trial and the gaps that would need configuration. Use the published plans or a regional proposal to confirm commercial scope.

Prepare a useful penetrant examination scope

Confirm a suitable nonporous surface and an examination objective involving surface-breaking discontinuities. Provide the material, surface finish, temperature conditions and any restrictions on inspection materials or cleaning products.

Understand the technique limitations

The approved technique governs preparation, penetrant application, removal, development and examination conditions. Contamination, smeared surfaces or unsuitable preparation can obstruct openings. Penetrant inspection cannot establish the condition of discontinuities that do not open to the examined surface.

Specify the records and review

Keep part identity, examination area, material system, procedure revision and indication locations in the report. Separate the observation of an indication from its evaluation against the specified acceptance criteria. Agree post-examination cleaning and handling with the owner.

For background, see ASNT’s method overview. Discuss procedure and personnel requirements before confirming the work.

/glossary/contrast.title: Radiographic contrast | Atlantis NDT Glossary
/glossary/contrast.description: Radiographic contrast is the difference in image appearance between adjacent areas. In a radiograph, it helps make a change in material thickness, composition or internal condition distinguishable from its surroundings.
/glossary/contrast.html:
Radiographic contrast

Radiographic contrast is the difference in image appearance between adjacent areas. In a radiograph, it helps make a change in material thickness, composition or internal condition distinguishable from its surroundings.

What it means in an examination

Image contrast alone does not establish whether an examination can reveal the required discontinuity. Spatial resolution, noise, geometry, exposure conditions and viewing conditions also affect interpretation. A strongly contrasted image can still fail to show a small or unfavourably oriented discontinuity.

Important distinctions

Keep object contrast separate from the contrast produced by the film or digital imaging system and its display. Digital windowing can change how an image looks; it does not recreate information that was never captured. Evaluate the image using the procedure and the required image-quality evidence, rather than visual attractiveness.

Using the term correctly

For an actual examination, record the technique and retain the relevant image-quality checks with the image. The responsible interpreter applies the specified acceptance criteria. Contrast is an image characteristic, not an acceptance limit by itself.

ASNT radiographic-testing overview · Radiographic testing guidance · Discuss an examination scope

/glossary/latitude.title: Radiographic latitude | Atlantis NDT Glossary
/glossary/latitude.description: Radiographic latitude describes the range of exposure or object-thickness variation that an imaging system can represent usefully under a defined technique. It helps explain why one exposure may show useful detail across some thickness changes but not others.
/glossary/latitude.html:
Radiographic latitude

Radiographic latitude describes the range of exposure or object-thickness variation that an imaging system can represent usefully under a defined technique. It helps explain why one exposure may show useful detail across some thickness changes but not others.

What it means in an examination

Latitude and contrast describe different aspects of an image. A system that can capture a broad exposure range still needs adequate contrast, resolution and signal quality for the inspection task. Avoid treating the ability to display a bright and a dark area as evidence that both areas meet the examination requirements.

Important distinctions

For digital radiography, distinguish captured detector information from display settings. Window and level adjustments change the presentation of recorded data; saturated or inadequately exposed regions may not contain usable information. The approved procedure and its image-quality checks determine whether the examination is acceptable.

Using the term correctly

When discussing a technique, specify the material, thickness range, geometry and imaging system. Keep the exposure and processing records needed to reproduce and review the image. Do not use a generic latitude value from a different system as an acceptance criterion.

ASNT radiographic-testing overview · Radiographic testing guidance · Discuss an examination scope

/glossary/se-75.title: Selenium-75 in industrial radiography | Atlantis NDT Glossary
/glossary/se-75.description: Selenium-75 is a radioactive isotope used as a gamma-radiography source in suitable industrial applications. Its use is a regulated radiation-safety activity, distinct from the interpretation of the resulting radiographic image.
/glossary/se-75.html:
Selenium-75 in industrial radiography

Selenium-75 is a radioactive isotope used as a gamma-radiography source in suitable industrial applications. Its use is a regulated radiation-safety activity, distinct from the interpretation of the resulting radiographic image.

What it means in an examination

Source selection depends on the component, material, thickness, geometry, required image quality and the authorised technique. A brief isotope description cannot establish a usable thickness range or an exposure time for a particular examination. Those decisions require the appropriate procedure, equipment information and qualified personnel.

Important distinctions

A sealed source continues to emit radiation without an electrical power supply. Source security, transport, storage, operation and emergency arrangements therefore require the controls applicable to the jurisdiction and the authorised organisation. A training article does not provide authority to possess or operate a source.

Using the term correctly

For procurement or inspection planning, ask the authorised provider to confirm source and equipment suitability, image-quality requirements, access constraints and the records supplied with the examination. Keep radiation-protection responsibilities separate from the customer’s acceptance criteria for the component.

/blog/digital-twins-reduce-refinery-turn.title: Digital Twins for Refinery Turnaround Planning | Atlantis NDT
/blog/digital-twins-reduce-refinery-turn.description: Use inspection-linked digital twins to prepare a refinery turnaround. Define the asset scope, validate records and measure planning effort without assumed savings.
/blog/digital-twins-reduce-refinery-turn.html:
Using digital twins to prepare a refinery turnaround

A refinery turnaround brings inspection, maintenance, access and production teams into the same planning exercise. A digital twin can help them find the records behind a work item and understand its location. Whether that saves time depends on the quality of the records, the workflow and the people maintaining the model. There is no universal percentage reduction that a project should assume.

This page covers setting up a measurable pilot. For the full planning picture, from scope built on inspection history to access planned in the model and NDT results recorded on the CMLs during the outage, read digital twins for turnarounds.

Start with a decision that currently takes too long

Choose a recurring task: locating a measurement point, retrieving the previous inspection report, checking whether a finding remains open, or assembling the evidence for a planned repair. Record the current process and the time spent on each step. This gives the pilot a defined purpose and a baseline.

Keep the boundary manageable. One unit or asset group with dependable identifiers is more useful for evaluation than a site-wide model whose inspection locations cannot be reconciled. Agree which decisions the model supports and which remain in the existing maintenance or document system.

Connect work items to traceable inspection records

Each work item needs a consistent asset and location reference. Attach the inspection date, method, source report and review status. Keep the original result and its limitations accessible. A planner should be able to distinguish an examined location from an inaccessible area or a location with no usable history.

Reconcile repairs, replacements and changed equipment tags before comparing measurements. If readings were taken at different locations or under different conditions, an apparent trend may be misleading. A visual model can display the evidence, but the responsible technical personnel determine what it supports.

Test the handover between teams

Ask an inspector to locate a finding, a planner to identify the associated work and a reviewer to retrieve the source record. Include an amended report and an unresolved action in the exercise. Check that users see the correct version and understand who can change the status.

Access preparation, isolation, permits and inspection sequencing remain project responsibilities. The model should make relevant constraints easier to find; it does not approve access or authorise continued operation. Record exclusions in the work scope rather than leaving them implicit.

Measure the pilot without inventing a return

Compare the same planning tasks before and after the pilot. Record retrieval time, missing or mismatched records, correction effort and the time required to keep the model current. Separate one-time data cleanup from recurring operating effort. If a different team or a different asset group is used, explain why the comparison is still useful.

Do not convert all saved administrative time into an assumed reduction in shutdown duration. The turnaround schedule may be governed by access, repairs, materials, production constraints or other critical work. A planning improvement has value even when it does not change the completion date.

Define what happens after the turnaround

Assign responsibility for importing final reports, closing findings and updating the asset history. Agree exports, backups, permissions and the link to the system that owns maintenance actions. A model that stops being maintained after the outage will become less useful for the next inspection cycle.

Refinery digital-twin scoping guide · Inspection reporting with asset context · Discuss a pilot using your records

/blog/adhesive-bond-line-inspection-tech.title: Adhesive Bond Inspection: Disbonds, Voids and Weak Bonds | Atlantis NDT
/blog/adhesive-bond-line-inspection-tech.description: Choose bond inspection around the joint design, reference specimens and detection limits. Understand why an ultrasonic image does not prove bond strength.
/blog/adhesive-bond-line-inspection-tech.html:
Adhesive Bond Inspection: Disbonds, Voids and Weak Bonds

An adhesive joint can contain a void, a separated interface or a weak bond that remains in intimate contact. Those conditions do not necessarily produce the same inspection response. A useful inspection plan begins by naming the condition it must detect, rather than asking for a general “bond quality scan”.

Separate missing adhesion from missing material

Ultrasonic inspection can help map changes at an interface, while other techniques may suit particular skins, cores or access arrangements. A clear image of a void is not evidence that every remaining part of the joint has adequate strength. NASA’s Orion heatshield work illustrates why intimate-contact unbonds can challenge conventional inspection.

Surface preparation, adhesive storage, mixing and cure records therefore remain part of the evidence. NDT cannot recover a missing manufacturing history or substitute for a qualified bonding process.

Demonstrate the technique on the actual joint

Document the adherend materials, thicknesses, adhesive layer, curvature and accessible surfaces. Ask whether the reference specimen represents those features and the flaw types of concern. A flat coupon with a convenient insert may not establish performance on a curved production assembly.

Agree the scanned area and how edges, stiffeners and inaccessible regions will be marked. Keep the original data and the settings needed to reproduce the examination.

Report what the result establishes

Distinguish an indication from a confirmed disbond, and an inspected area from an unexamined area. Record the location system, reference checks, indication dimensions and interpretation limits. The responsible engineering authority should define acceptance and any confirmatory work; a generic pressure-vessel or piping limit does not apply to an adhesive joint by default.

References and next steps

NASA’s Orion bond-inspection study provides further background. Use the governing specification and approved procedure for the actual job.

Discuss the examination scope. Include the component, material, service history and decision the inspection needs to support.

/blog/arc-flash-and-electrical-safety-in.title: Electrical and Arc-Flash Safety in an NDT Laboratory | Atlantis NDT
/blog/arc-flash-and-electrical-safety-in.description: Plan electrical safety for NDT benches, UV lamps and powered inspection equipment. Clarify isolation, qualified-person responsibilities and return to service.
/blog/arc-flash-and-electrical-safety-in.html:
Electrical and Arc-Flash Safety in an NDT Laboratory

An NDT qualification does not, by itself, qualify someone to work on electrical equipment. Magnetic-particle benches, industrial radiography equipment and ordinary laboratory power supplies need electrical controls appropriate to the task and installation.

Define the work before opening equipment

Separate normal operation, cleaning and maintenance from fault finding inside an enclosure. Identify who controls the equipment and who is authorised to isolate, test or repair it. Do not make an improvised repair merely because an inspection job is waiting.

OSHA’s electrical guidance addresses de-energisation, lockout and verification by qualified people. A switch in the off position is not sufficient evidence that an installation is safe. The site’s electrical programme must determine the applicable isolation and protective measures.

Include inspection-specific conditions

Wet-process benches, damaged lamp cables, temporary extensions and trailing leads deserve attention during the laboratory risk review. Arrange the workspace so liquid handling and component movement do not damage electrical connections. Remove suspect equipment from use and identify it clearly so another shift does not reconnect it.

The electrical assessment should also consider stored energy and equipment that has more than one supply. This article is a planning guide, not an instruction for testing live circuits or selecting protective clothing.

Make the handover explicit

Keep the equipment identifier, fault description, isolation responsibility and repair record together. Before returning a unit to NDT service, confirm both its electrical release and the method-specific performance checks required by the approved procedure. Electrical repair and inspection-system verification answer different questions; retain evidence of both.

References and next steps

OSHA’s electric-arc flash guidance provides further background. Use the governing specification and approved procedure for the actual job.

Discuss the examination scope. Identify the NDT equipment and inspection requirements. Electrical work must remain with the site’s qualified electrical personnel.

/blog/asme-pcc-3-in-service-inspection-p.title: ASME PCC-3: Inputs for Risk-Based Inspection Planning | Atlantis NDT
/blog/asme-pcc-3-in-service-inspection-p.description: Understand the scope of PCC-3 and the inspection evidence needed for a risk-based plan, including damage mechanisms, uncertainty and review triggers.
/blog/asme-pcc-3-in-service-inspection-p.html:
ASME PCC-3: Inputs for Risk-Based Inspection Planning

ASME PCC-3 concerns inspection planning using risk-based methods. It does not turn every NDT result into a remaining-life assessment, and it is not a general approval route for an AI inspection system. The practical starting point is a clearly bounded asset and a stated planning decision.

Prepare an evidence pack

Identify the equipment, materials, operating envelope, credible damage mechanisms and relevant inspection history. Keep the assumptions visible: missing thickness history and uncertain service conditions are different problems and should not be hidden behind a single risk score.

Describe the coverage and limitations of previous examinations. A nominal thickness value without a location, date and measurement basis is a weak input for a future inspection plan.

Connect the examination to the damage

Specify what the next examination is intended to detect or measure, where it will be performed and what would trigger follow-up. A method suited to general wall loss may not address a small crack in the area that controls the decision.

Inspection effectiveness should be justified for the expected condition and access. Do not infer capability from the method name alone. The responsible integrity team must also determine how regulations and the asset’s governing requirements constrain the plan.

Define who changes the plan

Record who owns the risk assessment, who approves inspection intervals and which changes require review. A process change, an unexpected indication or a newly inaccessible area can matter even if the previous inspection date has not expired. Atlantis NDT can discuss examination procedures and data records; an engineering RBI or fitness-for-service assessment needs its own competent, authorised scope.

References and next steps

ASME’s PCC-3 scope and contents provides further background. Use the governing specification and approved procedure for the actual job.

Discuss the examination scope. Include the component, material, service history and decision the inspection needs to support.

/blog/asme-section-ix-wps-pqr-welder-qua.title: WPS, PQR and Welder Qualification: Keeping the Records Separate | Atlantis NDT
/blog/asme-section-ix-wps-pqr-welder-qua.description: Understand how a welding procedure specification, procedure qualification record and welder qualification support different decisions under Section IX.
/blog/asme-section-ix-wps-pqr-welder-qua.html:
WPS, PQR and Welder Qualification: Keeping the Records Separate

Three records often arrive in the same welding dossier but answer different questions. The WPS tells production how to weld within an authorised range. The PQR records the conditions and results of a procedure qualification test. A welder or operator qualification concerns the person’s demonstrated performance within its qualified range.

Start with the governing construction requirements

ASME Section IX addresses qualification of procedures and personnel. Establish why it applies to the work and which edition the contract or governing code invokes. A qualification document alone does not establish every production-weld examination or acceptance requirement.

Before a job starts, compare the proposed production variables with the WPS and its supporting qualification basis. Resolve gaps through the responsible welding authority rather than changing a document after fabrication.

Keep the evidence traceable

Give each WPS a controlled identity and revision. Link the supporting PQR without rewriting the original test conditions to match a later production preference. Record the test reports and required approvals so a reviewer can follow the qualification evidence.

For a welder, maintain the qualification scope and applicable continuity records. A certificate photograph with no process, range or supporting record does not give a planner enough information to allocate the work.

Connect the dossier to the actual weld

The production record should identify the joint, drawing, material, WPS revision and welder or operator. Link subsequent NDT to that same joint identity. If a weld is repaired, preserve the original result and repair history instead of overwriting the first report. This makes a later review of fabrication and examination much more reliable.

References and next steps

ASME’s Section IX qualification overview provides further background. Use the governing specification and approved procedure for the actual job.

Discuss the examination scope. Bring the production requirement, relevant WPS, supporting qualification records and the specific gap you need to resolve.

/blog/asnt-recertification-pathway-2028.title: ASNT Renewal and Recertification: Prepare the Right Evidence | Atlantis NDT
/blog/asnt-recertification-pathway-2028.description: Plan ASNT renewal using your actual credential, expiry date and scheme requirements. Keep employer authorisation separate from central certification.
/blog/asnt-recertification-pathway-2028.html:
ASNT Renewal and Recertification: Prepare the Right Evidence

The first renewal question is the exact name of the credential you hold. An employer-issued NDT certificate, ASNT NDT Level III and an ASNT 9712 certificate do not share one universal renewal checklist. Start with the issuing body’s record and the expiry date shown for each method.

Check the scheme before booking training

Use ASNT Certification Services’ current renewal guidance for an ASNT-issued credential. It explains the relevant programme routes and documentation. Do not assume that a course automatically earns renewal credit or replaces an examination. Confirm eligibility and documentary requirements before paying for a course.

For employer-based certification, the employer’s applicable written practice governs the certification process. A centrally issued certificate may form part of that evidence, but the employer still needs to establish the authorisation required for the assigned work.

Build a file that can be checked

Keep the credential number, methods, level, expiry dates and issuing body together. Add evidence of qualifying activities, employment and other requirements that actually apply to your programme. Record dates and retain the original supporting documents; a total entered into a spreadsheet is difficult to verify on its own.

Leave time to resolve an incomplete application or an unavailable examination appointment. Training enrolment should not be treated as an extension to a certificate that has expired.

Keep the work roster current

Separate renewal progress from permission to perform or approve a job. If a credential expires or its scope changes, the responsible employer should review affected assignments. Atlantis courses are primarily self-paced, with year-round joining and Level III clarification support; confirm that the selected course fits your specific renewal objective.

References and next steps

ASNT Certification Services renewal guidance provides further background. Use the governing specification and approved procedure for the actual job.

Discuss a training or renewal preparation requirement. Bring the credential scheme, method, level and expiry date, together with your existing training and experience records.

/blog/compare-asnt-vs-cswiq-vs-iso-9712-.title: ASNT, CSWIP and ISO 9712: Which Requirement Does the Job Specify? | Atlantis NDT
/blog/compare-asnt-vs-cswiq-vs-iso-9712-.description: Compare employer-based NDT certification, central NDT certification and welding-inspection credentials without assuming they are interchangeable.
/blog/compare-asnt-vs-cswiq-vs-iso-9712-.html:
ASNT, CSWIP and ISO 9712: Which Requirement Does the Job Specify?

“ASNT or CSWIP?” is too broad to answer reliably. ASNT has publications and several certification programmes; CSWIP covers several occupational schemes; ISO 9712 is a standard for NDT personnel certification. Compare the exact credential required by the job, not only the organisation’s name.

Identify the role and examination method

A welding inspector’s duties differ from those of an ultrasonic testing technician. CSWIP welding inspection and CSWIP NDT certification are distinct schemes. A welding-inspection certificate should not be read as proof of qualification in every NDT method.

For an NDT role, record the method, level, sector and any technique limitations. Ask the employer which certificate scheme, written practice and customer approvals apply. Geography alone does not establish that a credential will be accepted.

Separate training from certification

A course completion record documents training. Certification also depends on the applicable scheme’s eligibility, experience, assessment and other requirements. Ask the training provider exactly which document is issued and which steps remain with the employer or certification body.

Employer-based certification under a written practice and central certification have different administrative responsibilities. Neither should be advertised as automatic permission to work for every employer or customer.

Compare a complete pathway

Before choosing a course, collect the target job specification and your existing training, experience and certification records. Identify the gaps method by method. Include practical assessment arrangements, application evidence and renewal obligations in the comparison. The useful outcome is a documented route to the required role, not a claim that one brand of certificate is universally best.

References and next steps

CSWIP’s scheme and qualification FAQs provides further background. Use the governing specification and approved procedure for the actual job.

Discuss the certification requirement in your job specification. Bring the target job’s qualification requirement and the training, experience and certificates you already hold.

/blog/iso-5817-weld-quality-levels-2028.title: ISO 5817 Quality Levels B, C and D: What They Mean | Atlantis NDT
/blog/iso-5817-weld-quality-levels-2028.description: Understand ISO 5817 weld quality levels and why the selected level, examination method and acceptance reference must be agreed before inspection.
/blog/iso-5817-weld-quality-levels-2028.html:
ISO 5817 Quality Levels B, C and D: What They Mean

ISO 5817 defines quality levels for imperfections in certain fusion-welded joints. Its published scope includes steel, nickel and titanium and their alloys, with beam welding excluded. The quality levels are B, C and D; B represents the highest requirements on the finished weld within this standard.

Find the specified level first

The inspector should not choose a quality level after seeing a result. Establish the level required by the drawing, product standard or contract, and the applicable edition. Where a project assigns different requirements to different joints, retain that mapping in the inspection plan.

A quality level is not a universal statement of fitness for every service condition. The standard concerns production quality and workmanship; the designer and governing requirements determine suitability for the application.

Use the right examination and acceptance reference

Agree which imperfections the examination is intended to reveal and which method-specific acceptance rules apply. A visual dimension and an ultrasonic response are different observations. Do not convert a UT amplitude directly into a workmanship limit without a valid basis.

Keep the examination procedure, coverage and reporting threshold distinct from the final acceptance decision. If the method cannot assess a specified feature, identify that limitation before declaring the joint acceptable.

Make the record reproducible

Identify the joint, drawing revision, specified level, examination method and reference used for the decision. Describe each reportable indication with its location and measured characteristics. Record any repair and re-examination against the same joint identity. Use a licensed copy of the applicable standard for limits; a short web summary cannot reproduce its tables and conditions.

References and next steps

ISO 5817: scope and published edition provides further background. Use the governing specification and approved procedure for the actual job.

Discuss the examination scope. Include the component, material, service history and decision the inspection needs to support.

/blog/ndt-calibration-laboratory-iso-170.title: Choosing an NDT Calibration Laboratory: Scope, Results and Traceability | Atlantis NDT
/blog/ndt-calibration-laboratory-iso-170.description: Check a laboratory’s accreditation scope, measurement range and calibration report before treating an NDT instrument as suitable for a job.
/blog/ndt-calibration-laboratory-iso-170.html:
Choosing an NDT Calibration Laboratory: Scope, Results and Traceability

A calibration sticker is a useful reminder, but it is not the complete evidence. When selecting a laboratory, start with the measurand, range and uncertainty your inspection work needs. Then check whether the proposed calibration service covers those requirements.

Read the accreditation scope

ISO/IEC 17025 addresses the competence and consistent operation of testing and calibration laboratories. An accreditation claim should be checked against the laboratory’s current published scope and the actual service ordered. Accreditation for one measurement does not establish competence for every instrument or range.

Specify the instrument identity, accessories, channels and functions that matter to your use. Agree whether adjustments are permitted and whether the report will distinguish the condition received from the condition returned.

Review the report before release

Check the equipment identifier, results, units, measurement conditions and uncertainty information relevant to the calibration. If a statement of conformity is requested, agree the specification and decision rule with the laboratory. An unexplained “pass” can leave the inspection team unable to judge suitability.

If the instrument was found outside the required tolerance, assess the effect on previous work through the quality system. Replacing the sticker does not answer that retrospective question.

Keep calibration and field checks separate

Laboratory calibration does not eliminate the equipment checks required by the NDT procedure. Retain those job checks with the instrument, probe or other relevant assembly used during the examination. Review recall intervals using applicable requirements, usage and performance history instead of assuming that one interval suits every item.

References and next steps

ISO/IEC 17025: laboratory competence requirements provides further background. Use the governing specification and approved procedure for the actual job.

Review calibration record management. Identify the instrument, measurement functions, ranges and calibration records your inspection procedure requires.

/blog/ndt-roi-calculator-digital-twin-vs.title: Digital Twin or Spreadsheet? Build an Inspection Business Case | Atlantis NDT
/blog/ndt-roi-calculator-digital-twin-vs.description: Estimate the cost of finding, reconciling and reviewing inspection records before buying a digital twin. Separate measurable benefits from assumptions.
/blog/ndt-roi-calculator-digital-twin-vs.html:
Digital Twin or Spreadsheet? Build an Inspection Business Case

A digital twin is worth evaluating when asset context changes how a team uses its inspection records. A spreadsheet can remain a reasonable choice for a small, controlled register. The business case should identify an operational problem and measure whether the proposed system solves it.

Measure the current work

Choose a representative inspection package and time the tasks that recur: finding the asset, matching a report to its location, reconciling revisions and preparing a review. Record how often the task occurs and which staff perform it. Include rework only where there is evidence; do not start with an assumed percentage saving.

Distinguish time that can actually be redeployed from small fragments that will not change staffing or throughput. A faster screen is useful, but it does not automatically create a cash saving.

Compare the full cost

Include data preparation, asset identifiers, model preparation, hosting, licences, training, administration and interfaces. Separate one-time implementation from recurring cost. If a model must be updated after a modification, identify who does that work and budget for it.

For a simple scenario, annual benefit equals evidenced time saved multiplied by the relevant labour cost, plus other independently justified benefits. Subtract recurring cost before considering recovery of the initial investment. Test low, expected and high cases rather than presenting one precise forecast.

Run a bounded trial

Use a real asset and a defined set of reports. Ask users to find a prior indication, compare revisions and export a handover package. Record failures, manual steps and time taken. Keep the decision criteria agreed in advance. Atlantis can discuss digital-twin scope and integrations; an assumed platform capability should be demonstrated before it enters the financial model.

References and next steps

ASNT’s overview of NDT methods provides further background. Use the governing specification and approved procedure for the actual job.

Discuss a representative digital-twin trial. Bring a representative asset register, inspection report and the workflow you want the pilot to improve.

/blog/ndt-safety-requirements-radiation-.title: Industrial Radiography Safety: What a Site Coordinator Must Confirm | Atlantis NDT
/blog/ndt-safety-requirements-radiation-.description: Prepare for industrial radiography by verifying the authorised provider, radiation protection responsibilities, site controls and emergency arrangements.
/blog/ndt-safety-requirements-radiation-.html:
Industrial Radiography Safety: What a Site Coordinator Must Confirm

Industrial radiography needs a radiation protection plan as well as an inspection procedure. A site coordinator should understand who controls the work, how other people will be kept clear and what happens if normal operations are interrupted. This guide is a procurement and coordination checklist, not a radiographer operating instruction.

Verify the provider and the jurisdiction

Confirm the authorisations that apply to the equipment and location, including any movement or temporary-site requirements. In the United States, the NRC’s industrial radiography toolkit identifies the relevant licensing framework, including Agreement State responsibilities. Do not assume that one authorisation covers every jurisdiction.

Identify the provider’s radiation safety contact and the site person responsible for coordination. Personnel certification in an NDT method is not a substitute for the radiation-safety requirements governing the operation.

Agree the site interface

Provide the provider with the layout, access routes, adjacent work, occupied areas and foreseeable changes during the shift. Confirm how access will be controlled and how nearby teams will receive the work notification. The authorised radiography team must establish the operational radiation controls from its approved arrangements.

Coordinate competing tasks and unexpected access requests through the named responsible people. Do not move barriers or allow a schedule change to bypass the agreed process.

Prepare for interruption and handover

Before work begins, establish the emergency contact route and the site’s role in an incident. Keep untrained personnel away from source-recovery or equipment intervention. Agree how the work area is handed back, who authorises return to normal activity and which records the customer receives. Safety requirements should be resolved before a production deadline makes them a negotiation.

References and next steps

NRC’s industrial radiography toolkit provides further background. Use the governing specification and approved procedure for the actual job.

Discuss the radiographic examination requirement. Identify the site, component and examination objective. Agree radiation-protection arrangements with the authorised provider and site coordinator.

/blog/rov-offshore-platform-inspection-2.title: ROV Inspection of Offshore Structures: Specify the Evidence | Atlantis NDT
/blog/rov-offshore-platform-inspection-2.description: Define an ROV inspection around asset locations, visibility, sensor capability and traceable findings. Separate video coverage from quantitative measurements.
/blog/rov-offshore-platform-inspection-2.html:
ROV Inspection of Offshore Structures: Specify the Evidence

ROV footage is useful only when the reviewer can establish what was inspected and where a finding belongs. For an offshore structure, plan the asset identifiers, coverage and evidence format before mobilisation. A long recording with uncertain location is difficult to compare with the next campaign.

Define the question for each location

Separate a visual condition survey from a thickness measurement, a marine-growth assessment or another instrumented task. State the component and area of interest, the required access and the expected deliverable. An ROV is a deployment platform; its presence does not establish the capability of the inspection sensor.

For quantitative examinations, agree the procedure, reference checks, positioning and contact requirements. Demonstrate that the proposed arrangement can collect usable data on the relevant geometry.

Plan for incomplete coverage

Visibility, current, obstructions and surface condition can limit the survey. Record those limits at the affected locations instead of giving the whole structure an undifferentiated “inspected” status. Establish the escalation route when access or data quality does not meet the plan.

Tie each observation to a component identifier and an understandable location reference. Retain contextual images as well as close views so a reviewer can identify the feature without relying on the pilot’s memory.

Deliver a record that supports follow-up

Issue an indexed finding register linked to video or image evidence, with the date, location, inspection technique and coverage limitation. Identify follow-up work separately from confirmed findings. The responsible structural or integrity authority should determine significance and disposition; video alone does not establish structural capacity or remaining life.

/blog/boiler-tube-and-heat-exchanger-ins.title: Boiler and Heat-Exchanger Tube Inspection: Choosing the Examination | Atlantis NDT
/blog/boiler-tube-and-heat-exchanger-ins.description: Select tube inspection using material, damage mechanism, access and reporting needs. Compare wall-thickness mapping, electromagnetic methods and visual evidence.
/blog/boiler-tube-and-heat-exchanger-ins.html:
Boiler and Heat-Exchanger Tube Inspection: Choosing the Examination

A boiler tube survey and a heat-exchanger tube examination can need very different inspection arrangements. Begin with the tube material, dimensions, service history and suspected damage. The cheapest available probe is not a reliable basis for choosing the method.

Separate the inspection questions

Determine whether the concern is wall loss, a crack, local erosion, deposits or another condition. A technique that screens for wall changes may not characterise every flaw orientation. Identify whether the result is intended to rank tubes, estimate remaining wall or support an engineering investigation.

Review previous leak locations and plugged-tube records alongside the inspection history. Keep the distinction between measured damage and a suspected mechanism that still needs confirmation.

Match the method to material and access

Conventional eddy current is widely used for suitable heat-exchanger tubing; other electromagnetic arrangements or ultrasonic techniques may suit different materials and objectives. Confirm the actual probe’s capability on the tube configuration rather than treating these methods as interchangeable.

Access, cleaning and probe travel affect coverage. Supports, tube ends, bends and obstructions can complicate interpretation or leave regions unexamined. Agree how those areas will appear in the report before quoting a percentage of tubes inspected.

Make the tube map the common reference

Use a verified tube numbering system and retain it across campaigns. Link each result to its tube, examined length, procedure and relevant limitations. Record follow-up examinations and the owner’s plugging or repair decision separately. A wall-loss estimate should not be presented as an automatic remaining-life calculation without the necessary engineering inputs.

/blog/bolted-joint-integrity-assessment-.title: Bolted-Joint Inspection: Cracking, Corrosion and Clamp Load | Atlantis NDT
/blog/bolted-joint-integrity-assessment-.description: Define what a bolted-joint assessment must establish and distinguish flaw detection from bolt preload, alignment and joint design checks.
/blog/bolted-joint-integrity-assessment-.html:
Bolted-Joint Inspection: Cracking, Corrosion and Clamp Load

A bolt can be free of a detectable crack and still be part of a leaking or poorly clamped joint. Bolted-joint assessment therefore starts with the failure concern: damage to the fastener, loss of section, assembly condition, movement or clamp load.

Keep the questions separate

Visual examination can document corrosion, damaged threads, missing components and evidence of movement. Suitable surface or ultrasonic examinations may address particular crack concerns. None of those observations alone proves that the joint has its required preload.

An ultrasonic bolt-load measurement is a different application from ultrasonic flaw detection. Its suitability depends on the bolt, reference condition, measurement arrangement and qualified procedure. Do not infer load from a generic NDT scan.

Review the joint as an assembly

Collect the bolt specification, joint drawing, service conditions and available installation records. Identify changes such as substituted fasteners, coatings, lubrication or repeated reuse for the responsible engineering team to evaluate. Access to one end of a bolt may not permit the examination needed for a suspected flaw.

Decide whether the joint can be examined in place and who controls any disassembly. Inspection should not lead to unauthorised loosening, tightening or loading of an operating assembly.

Report evidence without overstating it

Identify each fastener or location, the accessible surfaces and the examination limits. Distinguish an observed indication from an engineering conclusion about load capacity. Where a trend is required, retain the same location and measurement basis. Refer disposition, tightening requirements and continued-service decisions to the authority responsible for the joint.

References and next steps
