/blog/bridge-and-structural-steel-inspec.title: NDT of Bridges and Structural Steel: Plan Around the Detail | Atlantis NDT
/blog/bridge-and-structural-steel-inspec.description: Plan steel bridge NDT using fatigue-prone details, geometry, access and traceable locations. Separate examination results from structural assessment.
/blog/bridge-and-structural-steel-inspec.html:
NDT of Bridges and Structural Steel: Plan Around the Detail

“Inspect the bridge welds” is not a sufficiently defined NDT scope. A useful plan identifies the structural detail, suspected condition and consequence of missing it. The bridge owner’s inspection programme and engineering assessment determine which details need attention.

Start with drawings and service history

Identify the member, connection and weld detail on a drawing or location schedule. Review known repairs, previous findings and relevant loading history with the responsible engineer. An inspection location described only as “near the bearing” may be impossible to reproduce on the next visit.

Plan access, traffic management and safe working arrangements with the owner. Limited access should become a recorded coverage limitation, not an unqualified satisfactory result.

Choose the technique for the detail

Visual examination establishes surface condition and context. Appropriate surface methods can investigate accessible crack concerns; ultrasonic techniques may address internal conditions where material, geometry and access allow. FHWA provides technical resources for bridge NDE, including ultrasonic applications.

Coatings, weld shape, attachments and backing can affect interpretation. Demonstrate the proposed technique on representative geometry and agree the examination coverage before it is accepted as a substitute for another method.

Support a repeatable engineering review

Record orientation, length and location of reportable indications, with photographs and measurement references. Preserve the distinction between a finding, its interpretation and the owner’s structural decision. An NDT report does not independently establish bridge load capacity. Track follow-up examinations and repairs against the original detail identifier.

/blog/casting-internal-porosity-detectio.title: Detecting Internal Porosity in Castings | Atlantis NDT
/blog/casting-internal-porosity-detectio.description: Compare radiography and ultrasonics for casting porosity, with attention to section changes, material structure, reference standards and acceptance.
/blog/casting-internal-porosity-detectio.html:
Detecting Internal Porosity in Castings

Internal porosity is a casting condition, not a single inspection specification. The required examination depends on the alloy, manufacturing route, section thickness and function of the part. A pressure-retaining casting and a lightly loaded housing may have different acceptance requirements.

Choose evidence that answers the question

Radiographic techniques can show changes in transmitted intensity associated with internal discontinuities. Ultrasonic techniques can investigate suitable castings, but the material structure and geometry may limit penetration or interpretation. Neither method guarantees detection of every pore.

Separate a search for volumetric porosity from investigation of cracks or other discontinuities. Orientation and geometry influence detection, so one successful demonstration should not be extended to every flaw type.

Plan around difficult regions

Identify heavy sections, abrupt thickness changes, riser-removal areas and other locations the product specification requires. Document accessible surfaces and any regions where the chosen arrangement cannot establish the required coverage. If reference specimens or images are used, confirm that their application matches the specified material and technique.

An image should be evaluated using the applicable acceptance reference and its conditions. Avoid assigning an acceptance level from an unrelated product standard because the examples look similar.

Keep production and disposition traceable

Tie the report to the casting identity, heat or batch information and drawing revision. Record the examination arrangement, reference checks, findings and limitations. Where repair is permitted, preserve the original examination and repair record before re-examination. The responsible product authority decides whether the evidence supports acceptance, repair or further investigation.

/blog/flange-face-inspection-and-leakage.title: Flange-Face Inspection: Evidence for a Leaking Joint | Atlantis NDT
/blog/flange-face-inspection-and-leakage.description: Investigate a flange leak using face condition, alignment, gasket and assembly records. Understand where surface NDT helps and what it cannot establish.
/blog/flange-face-inspection-and-leakage.html:
Flange-Face Inspection: Evidence for a Leaking Joint

A flange leak does not establish that the flange contains a crack. The investigation may need to consider the face, gasket, alignment, bolting and operating history together. Agree who owns the joint assessment before separating the inspection into isolated tests.

Examine the condition you can actually see

After the owner has made the joint safe and authorised access, document the sealing face and adjacent areas. Record damage, deposits, corrosion and other relevant features with a location reference. Preserve useful evidence before cleaning or repair changes it.

Surface examination may help investigate a suspected surface-breaking discontinuity when the material and surface condition permit. It does not measure gasket compression or prove that the assembled joint will remain leak-free.

Keep dimensional and NDT evidence distinct

Face geometry, alignment and surface finish may need dimensional evaluation under the applicable specification. A penetrant or magnetic-particle examination answers a different question. Define the reference, measuring arrangement and acceptance responsibility for each activity.

Provide the assessor with the gasket identity, relevant assembly records and operating changes where available. Do not treat a successful NDT result as approval to reuse a gasket or return a damaged joint to service.

Make repair and handover traceable

Record the initial condition, authorised work and re-examination results against the same joint identifier. Any machining or other repair needs its own approved limits and acceptance basis. Keep the responsible engineering decision separate from the technician’s observations so the final dossier shows why the joint was accepted.

/blog/food-processing-equipment-ndt-and-.title: NDT in Food-Processing Plants: Inspectability and Hygiene | Atlantis NDT
/blog/food-processing-equipment-ndt-and-.description: Plan NDT around food-contact surfaces, cleaning, inspection materials and maintenance release. Separate crack examination from hygienic acceptance.
/blog/food-processing-equipment-ndt-and-.html:
NDT in Food-Processing Plants: Inspectability and Hygiene

Inspection in a food-processing plant must fit the site’s hygiene controls. Finding a discontinuity is only one part of the work: the team must also prevent inspection materials or equipment from contaminating the process and establish who releases the equipment back to production.

Agree the maintenance boundary

Identify food-contact surfaces, adjacent production and the approved shutdown or isolation arrangements. Ask the owner which cleaning, access and material controls apply. Bring the maintenance, quality and food-safety teams into the planning where their responsibilities overlap.

Record the inspection materials proposed for the job, including cleaners and couplants. Do not assume that a product acceptable for a workshop examination is suitable for this location or product stream.

Select a method for the actual condition

Visual examination may identify surface damage, weld profile concerns or inaccessible cleaning features. Suitable penetrant examination can address surface-breaking discontinuities, while ultrasonic techniques may answer particular wall or weld questions. Method selection must account for material, geometry, access and the owner’s restrictions.

A method cannot establish general hygienic suitability merely because no reportable indication was found. Surface finish, cleanability and microbiological release are separate assessments.

Close the job with two clear decisions

The inspection report should identify examined locations, methods, findings and limitations. The maintenance record should document any repair and required follow-up. The owner’s authorised team then confirms cleaning and return-to-production requirements. Retain those decisions separately so an NDT result is not mistaken for a food-safety release.

/blog/pipeline-corrosion-and-mechanical-.title: Pipeline Corrosion and Mechanical Damage: Define the Inspection Inputs | Atlantis NDT
/blog/pipeline-corrosion-and-mechanical-.description: Plan measurements for pipeline wall loss and mechanical damage. Keep flaw characterisation, engineering assessment and repair decisions separate.
/blog/pipeline-corrosion-and-mechanical-.html:
Pipeline Corrosion and Mechanical Damage: Define the Inspection Inputs

Corrosion and mechanical damage can coexist at the same pipeline location, but they are not interchangeable findings. An assessment may need wall thickness, surface condition, dent geometry and crack-sensitive examination. The integrity engineer should define which evidence is needed for the decision.

Establish the location and history

Tie the work to a stable pipeline reference and record the material, dimensions and relevant service information available. Review earlier in-line or direct examination results without assuming that their locations and sizing conventions are identical.

For an exposed site, the owner must establish excavation, access and operating controls. The NDT scope should identify what surface preparation is permitted and who authorises further work.

Measure each condition on a suitable basis

A thickness survey can characterise wall loss within its coverage and resolution. It does not automatically assess a crack associated with a gouge or dent. A geometric survey likewise describes shape but does not establish fracture resistance.

Agree the measurement grid or scan coverage, reference checks and coordinate system. Preserve the raw data and record areas that could not be examined. A single minimum reading can hide the shape and extent needed for engineering review.

Hand over findings without a generic safe-life claim

Report each condition and the relationships between them, with dimensions, orientation and examination limits. The responsible pipeline integrity authority should select the applicable assessment method and decide on operating restrictions, repair or monitoring. Atlantis NDT can discuss the inspection evidence; a remaining-life or fitness-for-service calculation requires a separately defined engineering scope.

/blog/power-generation-equipment-inspect.title: Power-Plant NDT: Plan the Outage Around the Component | Atlantis NDT
/blog/power-generation-equipment-inspect.description: Scope power-generation inspection using the component, damage concern and outage access. Avoid treating all plant equipment as one code or method.
/blog/power-generation-equipment-inspect.html:
Power-Plant NDT: Plan the Outage Around the Component

A power plant contains equipment with different materials, duties and governing requirements. A boiler pressure part, a turbine component and a structural support should not receive the same generic inspection specification. Start with the component and the decision the outage team must make.

Build the scope from service experience

Review operating history, previous findings, repairs and relevant recommendations from the responsible engineering or equipment authority. Identify the degradation concern for each location. Keep a distinction between a suspected mechanism and a condition already established by evidence.

Agree examination timing around access, cleaning and other outage tasks. A technique that requires an exposed surface cannot be assumed to cover an area that remains insulated or obstructed.

Demonstrate the examination capability

Choose the method and technique for the material, expected condition and geometry. Record the procedure, reference arrangement and personnel requirements. Specialised components may need manufacturer-specific or owner-approved practices; a generic ASME or ASTM list does not establish compliance.

State the limits of the examination, including unexamined regions and conditions that affect data quality. Resolve unacceptable coverage before the component becomes inaccessible again.

Give the outage team a usable handover

Use component and location identifiers that match the maintenance system. Separate immediately reportable findings, completed examinations and pending follow-up. Link repair and re-examination records without overwriting the original result. The owner’s authorised engineering team determines disposition and return to service; the inspection report should make that decision traceable.

/blog/pressure-vessel-inspection-and-com.title: Pressure-Vessel Inspection: Scope, Evidence and Disposition | Atlantis NDT
/blog/pressure-vessel-inspection-and-com.description: Prepare a pressure-vessel examination with asset records, damage concerns, coverage limits and a clear division between NDT and engineering disposition.
/blog/pressure-vessel-inspection-and-com.html:
Pressure-Vessel Inspection: Scope, Evidence and Disposition

A pressure-vessel inspection is more than a set of thickness readings. The owner must establish the governing requirements, inspection responsibilities and decisions the examination will support. Those requirements depend on the vessel, service and jurisdiction; one code label does not answer every question.

Review the vessel before selecting locations

Gather the available drawings, design information, material records, operating history and previous examinations. Review known repairs and changes in service. Identify the expected damage mechanisms with the responsible integrity team and use them to define examination locations and techniques.

Distinguish external access from an authorised internal inspection. Entry, isolation and other site controls belong in the owner’s work arrangements, not in an assumed NDT instruction.

Specify the required measurements and coverage

For wall loss, define the location system and the measurement or scan coverage. For a weld or suspected crack, specify a suitable examination and the applicable interpretation requirements. No single technique establishes every aspect of vessel condition.

Record obstructions, surface limitations and regions that remain unexamined. Keep the original data and reference checks so later reviewers can understand how the reported measurements were obtained.

Separate findings from continued-service approval

An NDT report should state observations, measured characteristics and the acceptance evaluation within its authorised scope. Remaining-life calculations, fitness-for-service assessment and operating decisions require the relevant engineering inputs and authority. If findings exceed the agreed criteria, identify the referral and follow-up rather than assigning a generic repair or retirement decision. Preserve the complete history after repair and re-examination.

References and next steps

ASNT’s overview of NDT methods provides further background. Use the governing specification and approved procedure for the actual job.

/blog/weld-inspection-acceptance-criteri.title: AWS and ASME Weld Acceptance: Find the Governing Requirement | Atlantis NDT
/blog/weld-inspection-acceptance-criteri.description: Choose weld acceptance criteria from the applicable construction or product requirements, then align the examination procedure and reporting evidence.
/blog/weld-inspection-acceptance-criteri.html:
AWS and ASME Weld Acceptance: Find the Governing Requirement

An indication is not acceptable or rejectable simply because a report mentions “AWS” or “ASME”. Both organisations publish multiple standards with different scopes. The governing document, edition, joint category and examination method must be identified before applying a limit.

Separate qualification, examination and acceptance

A welding procedure qualification supports the welding process within its qualified range. An NDT procedure defines how the examination is performed. Production acceptance comes from the applicable construction, product or contractual requirements. These documents are related but do not perform the same job.

ASME Section IX, for example, addresses welding, brazing and fusing qualification. It should not be presented as a universal table of production-weld NDT acceptance limits.

Check whether the methods are comparable

Visual, surface, radiographic and ultrasonic examinations reveal different characteristics. A radiographic image and a UT amplitude do not describe an indication in the same way. Use the method-specific rules invoked by the governing requirement rather than transferring a numerical limit from another method.

Where a specification permits a substitute technique, confirm the conditions for that substitution before examination. A method’s popularity or speed is not sufficient evidence of equivalence.

Document the decision path

Record the joint identity, governing reference and edition, procedure revision, examination coverage and reportable characteristics. State the acceptance basis used for the conclusion. Resolve conflicting contract references through the designated technical authority rather than choosing the less restrictive limit. If repair is required, keep the initial finding and subsequent examination linked to the same joint.

References and next steps

ASME’s Section IX qualification overview provides further background. Use the governing specification and approved procedure for the actual job.

Discuss the examination scope. Bring the joint drawing, governing specification, examination method and the acceptance question to be resolved.

/blog/asnt-snt-tc-1a-certification-requi.title: SNT-TC-1A Requirements — 2024 Edition Explained
/blog/asnt-snt-tc-1a-certification-requi.description: SNT-TC-1A 2024 explained: who certifies, Level I-III duties, training and experience hours by method, exams, vision, recertification and a 30-day plan.
/blog/asnt-snt-tc-1a-certification-requi.h1: ASNT SNT-TC-1A 2024 Requirements, Levels and 30-Day Study Plan
/blog/asnt-snt-tc-1a-certification-requi.html:
ASNT SNT-TC-1A 2024 Requirements, Levels and 30-Day Study Plan

ASNT SNT-TC-1A certification requirements

SNT-TC-1A is ASNT’s recommended practice for employer-based NDT certification. Each employer writes a written practice, approved by its NDT Level III, that sets training and experience hours, vision exams, general, specific and practical examinations, and recertification for every method and level. The employer, not ASNT, certifies its people.

What is SNT-TC-1A, and who issues the certification?

ASNT Recommended Practice No. SNT-TC-1A is guidance for employers that run their own NDT personnel qualification and certification programmes. ASNT lists the current document as the 2024 edition with Addendum and describes it as outlining recommended education, training and experience by method. It is a recommended practice, not a standard. ANSI/ASNT CP-189 is the ASNT standard that sets minimum requirements for the same employer-based model.

Under SNT-TC-1A, ASNT does not certify anyone. The employer certifies its own personnel against its written practice, and the certification belongs to that employer. ASNT has also pointed out that an employer-issued certificate must never carry the ASNT logo, and that some documents called “certificates” are only evidence that a training course was completed.

ASNT’s summary of the mandatory “shall” statements in SNT-TC-1A sets out what every programme needs:

  • a written practice for controlling and administering training, examination and certification;
  • review and approval of that written practice by the employer’s NDT Level III, and a copy kept on file;
  • in-house examination questions approved by the NDT Level III;
  • no candidate examining themselves, and no examination given by a subordinate;
  • periodic recertification of all NDT personnel.

The employer may adapt the detail, but it may not eliminate training, experience, examination or recertification from the programme.

The edition matters when a code calls up the document. HSB reports that the 2025 edition of ASME Section V references SNT-TC-1A-2024 in the version without the Addendum, and that a November 2025 Section V interpretation confirmed the written practice must meet the Errata but not the Addendum. Check which edition your contract, code and written practice name.

What can NDT Level I, Level II and Level III personnel do?

Certification is granted per method and per level, so one technician can hold Level II in UT and Level I in RT under the same written practice. The written practice assigns the duties; the table follows the level definitions in the recommended practice.

What each SNT-TC-1A level is qualified to do
LevelQualified to
NDT Level IPerform specific calibrations, examinations and evaluations by following written instructions, under the supervision the written practice specifies.
NDT Level IISet up and calibrate equipment, and interpret and evaluate results against the applicable codes, standards and specifications. Prepare written instructions, give on-the-job training to trainees and Level I personnel, and report results.
NDT Level IIIEstablish techniques, interpret codes and specifications, and designate the methods and techniques to be used. Train and examine Level I and Level II personnel, and approve the written practice and the examination questions.

For pay context, O*NET lists a median wage of $78,350 a year for Non-Destructive Testing Specialists (17-3029.01). The figure uses BLS data for the broader “Engineering Technologists and Technicians, Except Drafters, All Other” group, so it is an indication rather than a salary by level.

How many training and experience hours does SNT-TC-1A recommend?

SNT-TC-1A recommends hours for each method and each level separately; there is no single figure for “Level II”. The table lists the recommended minimum classroom training and experience in the method for Level I and Level II. Level III is not a further block of method hours: its eligibility combines education and experience, as described below.

Three points decide how the numbers apply to you. The employer’s written practice sets the binding hours, and it can require more than the recommended minimums. Experience means time spent performing the method, documented and verified by the employer. Classroom hours and experience hours are recorded separately, so a longer course does not replace logged experience, and simulator practice counts as training, not experience, unless the written practice allows it.

Work out the hours a technician still needs with the SNT-TC-1A hours planner, and see how they fit a course on the NDT Level 1 training and NDT Level 2 training pages.

Which examinations does SNT-TC-1A require?

For Level I and Level II, the written practice combines three examinations with vision checks. ASNT’s Materials Evaluation describes the same three types for SNT-TC-1A and CP-189: physical (visual acuity), written and practical.

  • General examination (written): the basic principles and theory of the method. SNT-TC-1A and CP-189 both refer to the ANSI/ASNT CP-105 topical outlines for this body of knowledge.
  • Specific examination (written): the equipment, techniques, procedures, codes and specifications the employer uses for its work.
  • Practical examination: the candidate operates the equipment used on the job, performs the method on representative parts by following the employer’s procedure, and records the results.
  • Vision examinations: near-vision acuity and colour contrast differentiation. ASNT’s Materials Evaluation states that SNT-TC-1A calls for the ability to read a Jaeger No. 2 test chart at not less than 12 in. (30 cm), in at least one eye, with or without corrective lenses, for all levels. Colour contrast differentiation is assessed as the employer determines for the method.

The written practice states the minimum number of questions, the passing grades, how the practical is scored and how often the vision examinations are repeated. Ask your Level III for the figures that apply to you rather than relying on another company’s written practice.

ASNT’s central route splits the work differently. For ASNT NDT Level II, ASNT administers a computer-based general exam and a specific exam per method, currently in MT, PT, RT, UT and VT, and ASNT states that employers carry out the visual acuity, practical and any job-specific exams. Practise for the written papers with the NDT practice tests.

How do you qualify as an NDT Level III under SNT-TC-1A?

SNT-TC-1A ties Level III eligibility to education and experience, and higher education reduces the experience required. The employer’s written practice sets the exact combination and the Level III examinations, and the employer certifies its Level III like any other level. ANSI/ASNT CP-189 goes further and requires Level III personnel to hold ASNT NDT Level III certification.

The ASNT NDT Level III certificate

ASNT NDT Level III is ASNT’s central certification, issued by ASNT to the individual. First-time applicants pass the NDT Basic examination and at least one method examination; the examinations are multiple-choice and computer-based. Experience must be in NDT, under qualified supervision and in the methods applied for:

  • four-year degree in engineering or physical science: at least 12 months (252 days) of experience;
  • two full academic years of engineering or physical science study: at least 24 months (504 days);
  • no college: at least 48 months (1,008 days).
ASNT NDT Level III examinations as published by ASNT, checked October 2026
ExaminationItemsTime allowed
NDT Basic1354 hours
Method: UT, RT or ET (also AE and LT)1354 hours
Method: MT, PT or VT (also IR and MFL)902 hours

ASNT NDT Level III is renewed every five years, by application with points or by examination. Prepare for the Basic and method examinations on the ASNT Level III training page. If your company needs a written practice written, reviewed or audited, see outsourced NDT Level III consulting.

How does SNT-TC-1A recertification work?

SNT-TC-1A requires all NDT personnel to be recertified periodically and recommends a maximum interval of five years, according to ASNT’s summary of the document. The written practice states the interval and what recertification requires.

Employer-based certification does not travel with the person. ASNT’s summary notes that it is deemed revoked when employment ends, so a new employer reviews the training and experience records and certifies the person under its own written practice. Keep your own copies of training records, experience logs and examination results.

ASNT’s central credentials follow ASNT’s rules instead: ASNT NDT Level II is renewed every five years by application with continued employment or by examination, and ASNT NDT Level III every five years by application with points or by examination.

SNT-TC-1A vs CP-189 vs ASNT central certification vs ISO 9712

Who sets the rules and who certifies, by scheme
SchemeWhat it isWho certifies
ASNT SNT-TC-1A (2024)Recommended practice: guidance an employer adapts into its written practiceThe employer
ANSI/ASNT CP-189 (2024)ASNT standard: minimum requirements for employer-based certification, building on SNT-TC-1A; Level III personnel hold ASNT NDT Level IIIThe employer
ASNT NDT Level II and Level IIIASNT central certification by examination; for Level II the employer still carries out the visual acuity, practical and job-specific examsASNT, to the individual
ISO 9712:2021 and ASNT 9712Third-party certification scheme; ANSI/ASNT CP-9712:2023 is the US adoption of ISO 9712:2021, and ASNT runs ASNT 9712 Level II and Level IIIAn independent certification body

The contract or client specification normally decides which scheme applies. For a fuller comparison, including ASNT 9712, see the ASNT certification guide.

30-day SNT-TC-1A study plan

This is a week-by-week study schedule for a Level I or Level II candidate preparing for the employer’s general, specific and practical examinations in one method while working. It organises study time. It does not shorten the training or experience hours your written practice requires, and your Level III decides when you sit each examination. Plan about an hour on working days and a longer session at weekends.

Week 1 (days 1–7): requirements and records

Read your employer’s written practice for your method and level, and list the classroom hours, experience hours, examinations and vision checks it requires. Enter your logged hours in the hours planner to see what remains. Collect your training records and experience log, and book a vision examination if yours is due. Start the theory: read the ANSI/ASNT CP-105 topical outline for the method and mark the topics you have not yet covered.

Week 2 (days 8–14): general examination topics

Work through the principles of the method topic by topic from the outline: physics, equipment, techniques, variables and limitations. End each session by writing a short summary from memory. On day 14, take a timed practice test for the method and list every topic you got wrong.

Week 3 (days 15–21): specific examination topics

Switch to the documents you work to: the employer’s procedure for the method, the referencing code or specification and its acceptance criteria. Write out the set-up, calibration and reporting steps in order. Ask your Level III which documents the specific examination draws on, and clear up anything you cannot explain in your own words.

Week 4 (days 22–30): practical rehearsal and review

Rehearse the procedure from set-up to report. Where the Practical NDT simulator offers your method, use it for instrument set-up, calibration and scanning discipline, then practise on your employer’s equipment and representative parts under supervision. Take a second timed practice test on day 27, revise the weak topics, and on days 29 and 30 check your records file: training hours, signed experience log and a current vision examination.

Frequently asked questions about SNT-TC-1A

Q1: Is SNT-TC-1A a standard?

No. SNT-TC-1A is a recommended practice: guidance that each employer adapts into its own written practice, which then becomes a mandatory requirement inside that company. ANSI/ASNT CP-189 is the ASNT standard for employer-based certification, and ISO 9712 is the international standard for third-party certification.

Q2: Does ASNT certify people to SNT-TC-1A?

No. Under SNT-TC-1A the employer certifies its own personnel against its written practice. ASNT issues its own central credentials, such as ASNT NDT Level II, ASNT NDT Level III and ASNT 9712, which it examines and issues to the individual.

Q3: Can a training course certify me to SNT-TC-1A?

No. A course provides classroom training hours and a record of completion. Certification follows only when your employer has verified your training and experience, you have passed the examinations its written practice requires, including the vision examinations, and the employer has issued the certification.

Q4: Which edition of SNT-TC-1A applies to my work?

The edition named in your written practice, contract or referencing code. ASNT lists the current document as the 2024 edition with Addendum. HSB reports that the 2025 edition of ASME Section V references SNT-TC-1A-2024 without the Addendum.

Q5: Does SNT-TC-1A certification transfer to a new employer?

No. Employer-based certification belongs to the employer that issued it, and the ASNT summary of the document notes that it is deemed revoked when employment ends. The new employer reviews your training and experience records and certifies you under its own written practice, so keep copies of your records.

Q6: How often is SNT-TC-1A certification renewed?

SNT-TC-1A recommends a maximum recertification interval of five years for all NDT personnel, and the written practice sets the interval and the requirements that apply to you. ASNT NDT Level II and ASNT NDT Level III certificates are renewed every five years under the ASNT rules.

Q7: What vision examination does SNT-TC-1A call for?

A near-vision acuity examination and a colour contrast differentiation examination. ASNT Materials Evaluation states that SNT-TC-1A calls for the ability to read a Jaeger No. 2 chart at not less than 12 in. (30 cm) in at least one eye, with or without corrective lenses. The written practice states how often each examination is repeated.

Q8: Does an employer Level III need an ASNT NDT Level III certificate?

Under ANSI/ASNT CP-189, yes: Level III personnel hold ASNT NDT Level III certification. Under SNT-TC-1A, the written practice of the employer sets the Level III education, experience and examinations, and the employer certifies its Level III.
